outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are likely late this afternoon and evening across parts of the northern High Plains. Large hail, strong wind gusts and perhaps a couple of tornadoes can be expected. Isolated severe storms are also expected across portions of the southern High Plains while strong storms may be noted across the Southeast.

sections.title: Northern High Plains
sections.text: Significant 12hr mid-level height falls are forecast to spread across the inter-mountain region into the northern High Plains of MT/WY tomorrow afternoon ahead of a strong short-wave trough. Lee cyclogenesis is expected over south-central MT early in the period with subsequent movement into southern SK during the late evening. Very little eastward progression of the High-Plains lee trough is expected as deep-layer flow remains decidedly meridional due to mid-continent blocking. As a result, a narrow corridor of modest boundary-layer moistening will extend north across the High Plains where mid-upper 50s surface dew points are expected prior to convective initiation. Latest guidance suggests strong boundary-layer heating will be noted from eastern CO - WY - MT and parcels should reach their convective temperature by 22z. Forecast soundings across eastern WY are quite unstable with MLCAPE values of 2000-2500 J/kg. Given the strong deep-layer flow, supercells are expected and very large hail could be noted. North-northeast storm motions will be noted into the evening hours but severe convection should struggle to move east of 102W longitude. Along with hail, some wind and tornado thre

sections.title: Southern High Plains
sections.text: Front currently draped across north-central TX is expected to move little during the day1 period with the wind shift forecast to extend near the I-20 corridor across the Big Country - TX South Plains during the afternoon. Strong surface heating across west TX and eastern NM will likely result in convective initiation along/near the front. While mid-level flow is not very strong (roughly 30kt at 500mb), a weak short-wave trough will likely approach this region by peak heating which should encourage upward-evolving thunderstorm complex. Large hail and wind are the primary threats with storms that form in this very buoyant air mass.

sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: Very slow-moving upper low over the TN Valley is actually forecast to retrograde slightly during the latter half of the period. Resultant mid-level height rises will be noted across the Southeast during the period. Even so, weak surface low is forecast to track along the front across southern GA before lifting into SC during the overnight hours. This boundary draped into the Carolinas should provide sufficient low-level convergence for convective development by mid day as temperatures warm into the upper 70s. Adequate deep-layer shear will likely exist for a few weak supercells capable of producing gusty winds, hail, and perhaps a weak tornado. ..Darrow/Moore.. 05/20/2020

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms appear most probable today over parts of the north-central and southern Great Plains.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A slow-moving, high-amplitude synoptic pattern will persist across the CONUS, featuring a deep trough and embedded cyclone over the West, and a temporary Rex block over the East. The latter will feature an anticyclone over the upper Great Lakes and Northeast, and a well-defined cyclone whose center should meander erratically over the middle TN area most of the period. Slight northwestward retrogression of the 500-mb low is possible tonight as a ridge to the northwest breaks down. Meanwhile, a separate cyclone will dig southeastward along the northern part of the BC coast from its current position offshore of the southern AK Panhandle. This should lead to open-wave devolving and ejection of the western CONUS cyclone/trough. By 12Z tomorrow, the latter trough at 500 mb should extend from a remnant low/ vorticity max over north-central MT, across western WY and the Four Corners, to Sonora. At the surface, 11Z analysis showed a quasistationary frontal zone extending from a low-pressure area over south-central GA east- northeastward off the southern NC coast, and southwestward to the Gulf Coast near MOB. The boundary then extended west-northwestward over east-central TX, then in two seg

sections.title: High Plains
sections.text: A narrow corridor of the Great Plains, from one international border to the other, will be under at least isolated and marginal severe- thunderstorm threat this afternoon into evening. Critical foci for convection will be the MT low, Pacific front and its merging with the lee trough over the northern/central High Plains, orographic lift with the post-frontal northerly component over southern MT, the lee trough/dryline farther south, and the southern frontal zone across portions of northwest TX. In general, strong directional shear will exist up and down the entire corridor, but with greater deep/bulk shear over the northern High Plains and considerably more moisture/instability across the TX part of the corridor. Eastward extent of the severe threat, especially over the central/northern Plains, will be constrained by a combination of meridional flow component and strengthening MLCINH with eastward extent, related to lower theta-e in continental trajectories recycled from behind the eastern CONUS mid/upper cyclone. The relative maxima in convective concentration and severe potential still appear to be across parts of the following areas. --- Eastern WY/southeastern MT/Black Hills --

sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: A large area of precip and embedded non-severe thunderstorms is ongoing across portions of eastern/southern GA, becoming broken northward over parts of upstate SC and adjacent northeastern GA. This activity and its associated cloud/precip shield will substantially modulate diurnal destabilization in its current position, and perhaps slightly eastward. The eastward extension of this activity, and/or isolated to widely scattered, additional thunderstorm development expected through the afternoon to its east along outflow/differential-heating/sea-breeze boundaries, will pose a marginal threat for damaging gusts, hail and perhaps a tornado. Rich low-level moisture in the warm sector, along with diurnal heating, will support a crescent of 1000-2000 J/kg MLCAPE, amidst 25-35-kt effective-shear magnitudes. In that environment, strong directional shear and the presence of boundaries will foster the potential for messy, short-lived supercells, but amidst a predominantly multicellular convective field. ..Edwards/Smith.. 05/20/2020

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected this afternoon and evening across a broad portion of the High Plains.

sections.title: Eastern Wyoming/southeast Montana and Black Hills
sections.text: Influenced by increasing forcing for ascent/strengthening southerly mid/high-level winds ahead of the ejecting Great Basin/northern Rockies upper-level trough, widely scattered thunderstorms are still expected to initially develop near the Laramie range as well as the mountains of southern Montana by around mid-afternoon. Semi-discrete supercells are initially expected as storms mature, with large hail the primary risk along with some tornado potential. Upscale aggregation and outflow mergers will occur by early evening coincident with a general increase in convective coverage with time across portions of east-central/northeastern Wyoming to near the Black Hills and eastern MT.

sections.title: West/northwest Texas
sections.text: Development/intensification of thunderstorms is still expected by mid/late afternoon along the north/south-extending dryline and especially across the Llano Estacado vicinity near/just north of a surface triple point and nearby front where low-level/deep-layer shear and buoyancy will maximize. Large hail will likely be the primary risk with initial intense supercell development. Storm mergers will occur over time and downdraft/outflow prevalence will support aggregating/upscale-growing clusters during the evening, with a severe hail/wind threat spreading southeastward toward the Rolling Plains/Big Country/west-central Texas.

sections.title: North Florida to coastal Carolinas
sections.text: A moist warm-sector air mass persists across the region on the eastern/southern periphery of a Tennessee Valley/southern Appalachians-centered vertically stacked cyclone. One focus for short-term severe potential will remain along the immediate South Carolina coast where the environment is conducive for an isolated damaging wind/brief tornado risk. A couple of severe thunderstorms could also occur near the effective boundary that extends southwestward across far southern Georgia and northern Florida.

sections.title: Louisiana
sections.text: Elevated thunderstorms are occurring at midday across west-central Louisiana. These storms may continue to regenerate and gradually build southeastward in vicinity of a front that extends roughly WNW/ESE across the region. Hail locally to marginally severe levels may continue to occur, and while not certain, a damaging wind threat may exist if storms development occurs into the warmer air along/just south of the boundary across southern Louisiana. ..Guyer/Squitieri.. 05/20/2020

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected this afternoon and evening across a broad portion of the High Plains.

sections.title: 20Z Outlook Update
sections.text: Minor southwestward expansions of severe probabilities were made in portions of southeastern Wyoming. Observations and satellite indicate low-level upslope flow against higher terrain, forcing initiation near the Laramie Range. These storms should continue to mature into clusters while moving northward/northeastward into moderate instability and strong shear, posing a wind/hail and isolated tornado threat. Refer to MCD 643 for additional information on the near-term severe threat in this area. Farther southeast, a cluster of storms have begun to forward-propagate eastward across southeastern Louisiana and vicinity near/just north of a surface boundary across the region. Enough shear/instability exists for an isolated hail/wind threat with this activity. Clouds and light rain appear to have kept portions of this boundary in south-central Louisiana inhibited from deep convective development and may do so through the remainder of the day. Additional storms in northwestern Louisiana have maintained themselves on the eastern extent of lapse rates exceeding 8C/km aloft, which may result in isolated instances of hail despite the elevated nature of the convection in that area. mesoscale_discussions.summary: A couple damaging wind gusts and perhaps a brief tornado may accompany some of the strongest storms through the rest of the morning into early afternoon. The best chance for a brief tornado will be in southeastern South Carolina.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A 700-300 mb stacked cyclone, currently centered over eastern TN, continues to meander over the Southeast. Small mid-level impulses continue to pivot through large-scale cyclonic flow, with one particular 500 mb vortmax approaching the GA/SC border, providing enhanced lift and continued convective development. Two concentrated areas of convection are ongoing, with the first being in southern SC, with the second along the GA/FL border. 12Z soundings modified by current observations and Mesoanalysis both depict buoyancy to be greatest across southern portions of SC, with up to 1000 J/kg MLCAPE noted. Over 150 m2/s2 0-2 km SRH are also present across the area, with the current buoyancy/shear parameter space supporting some potential for updraft rotation. A few transient supercell structures have recently been observed via KCLX WSR-88D data, and a brief tornado cannot be completely ruled out. Farther south across the FL/GA border, convection may persist along the periphery of a moist, heated airmass. Here, water-loaded downdrafts may encourage a few damaging gusts with the more persistent storms.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to increase over the next couple of hours. Large hail and locally damaging wind gusts are possible. A watch will likely be needed by 20z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A surface low near the southeast MT/northeast WY border, east of the Big Horn mountains, was noted in 18z mesoanalysis. A strong baroclinic zone across the High Plains as allowed modest surface moisture to spread across the region on gusty southeasterly low level winds. Surface dewpoints are generally in the 50s to the east of a dryline/surface trough extending southward across eastern WY into eastern CO. Strong heating has allowed temperatures to warm into the upper 70s to low 80s beneath a plume of steep midlevel lapse rates of 7.5-8.5 C/km. As a result, moderate destabilization is occurring, with MLCAPE values increasing to around 1500 J/kg. Recently, vertically developing CU has been noted across parts of southeast WY over the higher terrain of the Laramie Range, but also further east near the dryline/surface trough near Platte and Goshen Counties. Water vapor satellite loops suggest stronger ascent is now spreading northeast across parts of western CO/WY and convective initiation is likely in the next couple of hours. Initially storms will likely develop off the higher terrain and shift northeast in the vicinity of the surface trough across east-central and northeast WY. Additional storms are expected to develop southward later this afternoon/evening into portions of southeast WY/far northeast CO and the western NE Panhandle as a cold front overtakes the dryline and develops eastward as the western upper trough ejects eastward. Shear profiles will strengthen with time, with effective shear greater than 40 kt and moderately long, straight hodographs favoring cells capable of large hail initially. A deeply mixed boundary layer resulting in steep low level lapse rates will allow for strong downdrafts capable of locally damaging winds. Storm clusters will likely experi

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to increase across eastern MT over the next couple of hours. Large hail and locally damaging wind gusts will be possible with these storms, and a watch will likely be needed by 21z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early-day showers and cloudiness has lifted northward toward the MT/SK border, allowing temperatures to quickly warm into the mid 70s to low 80s across much of eastern MT. Strong southeasterly low level winds ahead of a surface low just east of the Big Horn mountains have allowed surface dewpoints to increase into the mid 50s to near 60 F beneath steep midlevel lapse rates (7.5-8.5 C/km). Thunderstorms have already developed over the higher terrain of the Beartooth/Absaroka mountains, and an increase in CU has been noted in visible satellite imagery beneath scattered mid-upper level clouds. Increasing ascent is currently spreading into southern MT as a lead shortwave impulse ejects north/northeastward from the upper low centered over the northern Great Basin. This should result in additional storms developing over the higher terrain of southeast MT in the next couple of hours, as well as additional development further east across the High Plains of eastern MT as weak capping erodes. Strong effective shear will support organized cells/clusters with long, straight forecast hodographs indicating large hail potential when combined with thermodynamic characteristics across the region. Inverted-v sub-cloud thermodynamic profiles suggest strong downburst winds also will be possible. Clusters of storms will track generally northward during the evening and should mainly stay confined to eastern MT and far northwest SD.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An increase in storm coverage and intensity is expected over the next few hours. Storms may pose a severe hail threat early on, including the possibility of 2+ inch stones. A tornado also cannot be ruled out, especially with storms traversing a baroclinic zone. Upscale growth into one or more intense clusters is possible, where damaging winds may also become a concern. A WW issuance will be needed shortly.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong diurnal heating and weakening convective inhibition ahead of a dryline has recently encouraged the development of a CU field across west TX, where convective initiation is underway. Glancing upper-level support from a mid-level trough to the northwest, combined with continued boundary layer mixing should support increasing convective coverage through the evening hours. A relatively weak vertical wind field (below 300 mb) across much of west TX is in place, with bulk effective shear values remaining under 30 knots. As such, mainly multicellular convection is expected, with a transient supercell possible. Very steep deep-layer lapse rates exceeding 8.5 C/km will support MLCAPE/MUCAPE values above 2000/3000 J/kg. Severe hail may accompany the more organized cells/clusters, with a couple instances of 2+ inch diameter stones possible. In addition, visible satellite and surface METAR observations depict a differential heating boundary across southern parts of northwest TX. Here, locally higher effective SRH (100+ m2/s2) is present, based on RAP forecast soundings and Mesoanalysis. Any transient supercell structure traversing this boundary may acquire brief deep-layer rotation, supporting an enhanced threat for significant severe hail, damaging winds, and perhaps a tornado. Weak deep-layer shear and ample evaporative cooling in a dry sub-cloud layer may allow for efficient cold pool mergers and upscale growth into one or more relatively short-lived MCSs, as supported by CAM guidance. Damaging gusts may accompany this activity.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A storm or two may become strong enough to support large hail and perhaps a tornado.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong heating and an upscale component of flow have resulted in a deepening CU field across parts of far southeast Colorado. Capping remains rather stout across the central High Plains compared to regions farther south, raising doubts regarding the extent of convective coverage. In addition, vertical wind fields and associated deep-layer shear are weak, potentially limiting a more robust severe threat. Nonetheless, 8+ C/km mid-level lapse rates atop an adequately moist boundary layer support 1500+ J/kg MLCAPE. Upslope southeasterly flow with ample veering above 700 mb also yields curved hodographs, with up to 200 m2/s2 effective SRH. Should a storm initiate and become sustained, transient supercell structure may be achieved, with severe hail and perhaps a tornado possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms will pose a threat for hail and wind as they slowly move east and cross the Rio Grande in the Del Rio, TX vicinity. A watch is not likely due to the isolated threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms developing off the higher terrain of the Sierra del Carmen mountains in northern Mexico will continue gradually propagating east over the Rio Grande near Del Rio, TX in the next few hours. Although deep layer wind shear is weak (effective bulk wind shear near 20 knots) and outrunning outflows have been noted from KDFX, moderate MLCAPE values between 3000-3500 J/kg suggest that severe hail will be possible with any robust updraft that develops along the periphery/outflow of existing convection. Low-level lapse rates between 7-8 C/km in the 0-1 km layer may allow for some evaporative cooling and downdraft acceleration that could lead to damaging winds. While individual storms should be short-lived, additional development along outflows should continue for the next few hours before loss of daytime heating and boundary layer stabilization inhibits lift along any outflow boundary. Due to the isolated nature of the threat, a watch is not likely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat is shifting into the eastern parts of ww195.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Deep convection that initiated off the Laramie Range a few hours ago has since progressed across the High Plains of eastern WY. This activity has evolved into a squall line that is propagating through an instability axis near the WY/SD/NE border. While LLJ should encourage continued eastward movement, the corridor of appreciable buoyancy remaining is roughly 50-100 mi wide. For these reasons, severe threat appears to be peaking and will likely decrease between 103-102W longitude. ..Darrow.. 05/20/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for severe hail and wind will continue from Lubbock, TX southward into southwest TX. While a near term threat will continue for the Texas Panhandle, the overall severe threat is diminishing.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent radar imagery from the TX Panhandle southward into the eastern Big Bend region shows continued thunderstorm propagation along outflow boundaries from an initial round of convection that initiated off a now-retreating dryline. Given moderate instability near 3000 J/kg, but relatively weak effective bulk wind shear, the expectation for the coming hours is that thunderstorms will continue to develop along outflow boundaries and gradually propagate towards the eastern edge of WW 196. This is especially true from the Lubbock, TX area southward where instability is more favorable for continued storm development. The severe threat should continue for at least 1-2 hours after sunset before increasing inhibition limits lift along outflow boundaries. Further north into the TX Panhandle, MLCAPE is confined to a narrow corridor along the western edge of the Panhandle near the retreating dryline. Gravity waves noted in KAMA velocity data and GOES visible imagery suggest that inhibition is also stronger in this region and is mitigating more widespread storm development. Although a severe threat continues with ongoing convection and potentially from any northward moving left splits from west-central TX, inhibition will continue to increase and diminish the severe threat heading into the evening hours. ..Moore.. 05/21/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat should spread northeast across ww197.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Water-vapor imagery depicts a short-wave trough ejecting northeast across WY toward eastern MT. Large-scale forcing for ascent appears to be aiding broken squall line as it propagates across the plains toward a corridor of modest instability over eastern portions of ww197. With LLJ expected to increase across western ND into southeast SK later this evening, this convection should spread toward the international border into portions of extreme western ND. Latest hail algorithm output continues to suggest large hail is noted with supercell structures and this should be the primary concern, though some wind is also possible. ..Darrow.. 05/21/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat continues for the next few hours along a narrow corridor from northeast Colorado to the Nebraska Panhandle.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection that developed over the Laramie Range has propagated into western SD and weakened considerably, arcing southwest into northeast CO. This activity has overturned the narrow corridor of instability north of the CO border. As a result, strongest convection has lingered along the southwestern flank into Weld County CO where instability has yet to be overturned. Given the lack of large-scale support, this convection should move slowly southeast and gradually weaken over the next few hours. ..Darrow.. 05/21/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe thunderstorms continue, but will continue to become more isolated and sporadic in nature through 05 UTC.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regional radar and GOES IR satellite imagery continues to show thunderstorms ongoing along outflow boundaries from early convection. Storms south of the I-40 corridor have exhibited a gradual weakening trend per radar, satellite, and lightning data, but pockets of 1000-2000 J/kg MLCAPE and 30-40 knots of effective bulk shear may allow for periodic intensification that will pose a hail and wind threat over the next hour or so. Increasing inhibition with further loss of daytime heating within this area should contribute to a diminishing severe threat and inhibit widespread additional convective development. Further south towards San Angelo, TX, cold pool amalgamation within a cluster of thunderstorms has supported continued convective development to the east/southeast despite increasing inhibition. This trend is reflected in recent GOES IR imagery, and an increasing low-level jet through the next 1-3 hours will promote continued storm development to the south/southeast. Despite weak bulk shear, 2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE will continue to pose an isolated hail threat with the strongest updrafts. While damaging wind gusts remain possible, the probability of widespread damaging winds will diminish as the boundary layer becomes decoupled. ..Moore.. 05/21/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging winds and hail are possible with a squall line as it races north toward the international border.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MCS has evolved over northeast MT this evening with an apparent MCV forming over southeast Garfield County. Latest radar data suggests an east-west squall line has begun to surge in excess of 50kt as it propagates north across McCone County -- just east of the evolving MCV. While some hail remains possible, severe winds are likely the main threat with this squall line as it surges toward the SK border. ..Darrow.. 05/21/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Transient/weak rotation may occur with more persistent storms moving from the shelf waters to the immediate coast.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar imagery during the past hour has shown weak/transient supercell structure near the Cape Fear vicinity. Despite surface conditions with temperature/dewpoint near 70 deg F, relatively cool mid-level temperatures are resulting in moderate buoyancy. Some enlargement of the hodograph due to veering/strengthening low-level flow with height, has yielded sufficient overlap of shear/adequate buoyancy near the immediate coast. Given this confined zone of instability/shear near the coast, another 1-2 weakly rotating cells cannot be ruled out during the next few hours near the Onslow Bay coast. ..Smith.. 05/21/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
